hints.title: Retaining Unmatched Bonus Records
hints.text: Employees without any recorded incentive must still be reported alongside those whose amount falls below one thousand.

hints.title: Left Outer Join and Null Checking
hints.text: Connect Employee to Bonus using a left join on empId. Employees lacking bonus records will produce null values in the bonus column.

hints.title: Predicate Disjunction Blueprint
hints.text: Filter with where bonus < 1000 or bonus is null. Select employee name and bonus amount.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT e.name, b.bonus
FROM Employee e
LEFT JOIN Bonus b ON e.empId = b.empId
WHERE b.bonus < 1000 OR b.bonus IS NULL;
```

complexity.notes: Left outer join preserving unmatched employee entries.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: An inner join drops employees who have no bonus record at all, violating problem requirements.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Outer join evaluates in linear time and yields null for non-existent bonus foreign keys.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explicitly testing for bonus is null because standard comparisons like < 1000 evaluate to unknown for null.

import pandas as pd

def employee_bonus(employee: pd.DataFrame, bonus: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = employee.merge(bonus, on='empId', how='left')
    filtered = merged[(merged['bonus'] < 1000) | (merged['bonus'].isna())]
    return filtered[['name', 'bonus']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Left Merge with Null Filtering
